<thought>
The 1H NMR shows:
- 1.20 ppm (d, J = 7.1 Hz, 3H): methyl group coupled to one proton (CH3-CH)
- 2.85 ppm (d, J = 6.9 Hz, 2H): CH2 group coupled to one proton
- 3.09 ppm (qdd, J = 7.1, 6.9, 6.9 Hz, 1H): CH group coupled to both the methyl and CH2
- 3.81 ppm (s, 3H): methoxy group (OCH3)
- 7.15 ppm (ddd, J = 8.5 Hz, 2H): aromatic protons (para-substituted pattern)
- 7.92 ppm (ddd, J = 8.5 Hz, 2H): aromatic protons (para-substituted pattern)

This suggests:
- A para-disubstituted benzene ring (4H in aromatic region with characteristic pattern)
- A methoxy group (3H singlet at 3.81 ppm)
- An isobutyl-like fragment: CH3-CH-CH2-

The aromatic signals at 7.15 and 7.92 ppm suggest an electron-withdrawing group on one side and possibly an electron-donating group on the other side of the benzene ring.

Let me get the 13C NMR to confirm the structure.
</thought>
<action>carbon_nmr_spectra</action>

<thought>
The 13C NMR shows 11 distinct carbon signals (though some appear twice due to symmetry):
- 166.40 ppm: carbonyl carbon (C=O), likely an ester
- 144.78 ppm: aromatic carbon (possibly attached to electron-donating group)
- 132.00 ppm: aromatic carbon
- 130.07 ppm (appears twice): aromatic CH carbons
- 127.80 ppm (appears twice): aromatic CH carbons
- 52.24 ppm: methoxy carbon (OCH3)
- 49.55 ppm: CH carbon
- 43.55 ppm: CH2 carbon
- 19.23 ppm: CH3 carbon

This confirms:
- An ester group (C=O at 166.40 ppm, OCH3 at 52.24 ppm)
- A para-disubstituted benzene ring
- An isobutyl group: CH3-CH-CH2-

The structure appears to be: isobutyl 4-methoxybenzoate or similar.

Wait, let me reconsider. The molecular weight is 192.11. Let me calculate:
- Benzene ring: C6H4 = 76
- Ester group: CO2 = 44
- Methoxy on benzene: OCH3 = 31
- Isobutyl: C4H9 = 57

Total: C6H4 + CO2 + OCH3 + C3H7 = C10H12O3 = 180

That doesn't match. Let me reconsider the structure.

Looking again at the NMR:
- The aromatic pattern shows 4H in a para-substituted pattern
- One substituent is likely -CO2CH3 (ester with methoxy at 3.81 ppm and carbonyl at 166.40 ppm)
- The other substituent connects to the isobutyl chain

The isobutyl fragment: CH3-CH-CH2- connects to the benzene ring.

So the structure is: 4-(2-methylpropyl)benzoic acid methyl ester
Or: methyl 4-isobutylbenzoate

Let me verify: C6H4 + CO2CH3 + CH2CH(CH3)2 = C12H16O2 = 192.21

That matches! The SMILES would be: CC(C)CC1=CC=C(C=C1)C(=O)OC
